prompt:
You are judging which existing Allied Telesis test scripts cover a required test-step sequence.
For each candidate script decide whether it does ALL, SOME, or NONE of what the sequence needs.

## Required sequence (case AWPTCM-T33235)

1. action: Configure interface <port> speed 1000 duplex full.
   verify: Parse 'show interface <port>' output: speed=1000, duplex=full, state=up. Send Scapy/tcpdump traffic and verify count>0 with zero errors. self.passed() if all match, else self.failed().

2. action: Configure interface <port> speed 100 duplex full.
   verify: Parse 'show interface <port>' output: speed=100, duplex=full, state=up. Send Scapy/tcpdump traffic and verify count>0. self.passed() if all match, else self.failed().

3. action: Configure interface <port> speed 10 duplex full.
   verify: Parse 'show interface <port>' output: speed=10, duplex=full, state=up. Send Scapy/tcpdump traffic and verify count>0. self.passed() if all match, else self.failed().

4. action: Configure interface <port> speed 100 duplex half.
   verify: Parse 'show interface <port>' output: speed=100, duplex=half, state=up. Send Scapy/tcpdump traffic and verify count>0. self.passed() if all match, else self.failed().

5. action: Configure interface <port> speed 2500 duplex full (unsupported).
   verify: Parse 'show interface <port>' output: state=down or mismatch reported. Verify no traffic passes. self.passed() if link down, else self.failed().

6. action: Remove and re-insert cable/SFP on <port>.
   verify: Monitor 'show interface <port>' state: transitions down then up. Verify speed config remains fixed. self.passed() if state transitions correctly and config retained, else self.failed().

7. action: Execute 'show interface <port>' and 'show status'.
   verify: Parse CLI output to confirm speed, duplex, and link state fields exactly match configured fixed values. self.passed() if exact match, else self.failed().

- id: art/1334_epsr/test-1334.3001.py
  db: art | suite: 1334_epsr | cases: 
  title: EPSR - Super Loop Protection - transit node with single port on shared segment sends a link down message when shared segment goes down only to highest priority domain master, for each shared group of 
  summary: Tests EPSR Super Loop Protection and Enhanced Recovery on shared-segment transit/master nodes, verifying link-down, link-forward-request, and permission-link-forwarding messages.
  tags: epsr, vlan, traffic-generation
  case descriptions:
    * EPSR - Super Loop Protection - transit node with single port on shared segment sends a link down message when shared segment goes down only to highest priority domain master, for each shared group of datavlans
    * EPSR - Super Loop Protection - transit node with EPSR instances on a shared segment. When ports on non-shared segments go down, sends a link down for each EPSR Instance as expceted.
    * EPSR - Super Loop Protection - transit node with EPSR instances on a shared segment. When port on shared segment comes up & Health checks circulated,  EPSR is in blocking state. Ring up on higher priority EPSR instance brings port up. Ring up on lower priority does not bring port up.
    * EPSR - Super Loop Protection - higher priority master/lower priority transit  node with primary  port on shared segment. Shared segment ethA goes down . Expect Ringdown Flush DB, and unblocked secondary port on high prioirty ethC. Nothing on lower priority EPSR ethA
    * EPSR - Super Loop Protection - High priority master/ lower prioirty transit node with EPSR instances on a shared segment. When ports on non-shared segments go down, sends a link down for lower priority, and a ring down flush db for higher EPSR Instance.
    * EPSR - Enhanced Recovery Enabled - transit node (priorities set) when a port comes up with enhanced recovery enabled, a Link Forward Request is transmitted
    * EPSR - Enhanced Recovery - transit node with EPSR instances (priorities set).  When port goes down and comes up again, if a Permission Link Forward is sent in response to a Link Forward Request, the port goes forwarding.
    * EPSR - Enhancd Recovery Enabled - transit node with no priority set - when a port comes up with enhanced recovery enabled, a Link Forward Request is transmitted
    * EPSR - Enhanced Recovery  - transit node with EPSR instances. No priority set.  When port goes down and comes up again, if a Permission Link Forward is sent in response to a Link Forward Request, the port goes forwarding.
    * EPSR - Enhanced Recovery Enabled - Master node (priorities set) when a Link Forwarding Request is received up with enhanced recovery enabled & no Health Checks are circulating -  a Permission Link Forwarding is transmitted
